## pandas

```python
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("sales.csv", parse_dates=["date"])

df.head(); df.info(); df.describe()       # first look
df["region"].value_counts()               # category counts
df.isna().mean()                          # share missing per column

df[df.amount > 100]                       # filter rows
df.query("amount > 100 and region == 'TX'")
df.loc[:, ["date", "amount"]]             # select columns

df["month"] = df.date.dt.to_period("M")   # new column
df.groupby("region").amount.agg(["sum", "mean", "count"])
df.pivot_table(index="month", columns="region",
               values="amount", aggfunc="sum")

df.merge(customers, on="customer_id", how="left")
df.sort_values("amount", ascending=False)
df.fillna({"amount": 0}).drop_duplicates()
df.to_parquet("sales.parquet")            # fast, typed storage
```

## NumPy

```python
import numpy as np
a = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
a.shape, a.dtype, a.T                      # shape, type, transpose
np.zeros((3, 4)); np.ones(5); np.arange(0, 10, 2)
np.linspace(0, 1, 5)                       # 5 evenly spaced values

a.sum(axis=0); a.mean(axis=1); a.max()     # reductions
a @ a                                      # matrix multiply
np.where(a > 2, 1, 0)                      # vectorised if-else
a[a > 2]                                   # boolean mask

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)            # reproducible random
rng.normal(0, 1, 1000); rng.integers(0, 10, 5)
np.percentile(x, [5, 50, 95])
```

## SQL

```sql
-- top 5 regions by revenue in 2026
SELECT region,
       SUM(amount)        AS revenue,
       COUNT(*)           AS orders,
       AVG(amount)        AS avg_order
FROM   sales
WHERE  order_date >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP  BY region
HAVING COUNT(*) > 100
ORDER  BY revenue DESC
LIMIT  5;

-- join + window function: each order's share of its region
SELECT s.order_id, c.segment, s.amount,
       s.amount / SUM(s.amount) OVER (PARTITION BY s.region)
         AS share_of_region
FROM   sales s
LEFT   JOIN customers c ON c.id = s.customer_id;
```

## scikit-learn

```python
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.compose import make_column_transformer
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, OneHotEncoder
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingClassifier

prep = make_column_transformer(
    (StandardScaler(), ["age", "income"]),
    (OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore"), ["plan"]))
model = make_pipeline(prep, HistGradientBoostingClassifier())

Xtr, Xte, ytr, yte = train_test_split(
    X, y, test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=0)
cross_val_score(model, Xtr, ytr, cv=5, scoring="roc_auc")
model.fit(Xtr, ytr)
proba = model.predict_proba(Xte)[:, 1]
```

## Git

```bash
git clone <url>                 # copy a repository
git status                      # what changed?
git switch -c feature/churn     # new branch
git add notebook.ipynb src/     # stage changes
git commit -m "Add churn baseline"
git pull --rebase               # get others' work
git push -u origin feature/churn
git log --oneline --graph -10   # recent history
git restore file.py             # discard local edits
```

## Docker

```bash
docker build -t myapi:1.0 .            # build image
docker run -d -p 8000:8000 myapi:1.0   # run container
docker ps                              # running containers
docker logs -f <id>                    # follow logs
docker exec -it <id> sh                # shell inside
docker compose up -d                   # multi-container app
docker system prune                    # free disk space
```

## 🧮 Statistics formula sheet

| Concept | Formula | Plain words |
|---|---|---|
| Mean | $\bar x = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n x_i$ | The balance point |
| Sample variance | $s^2 = \frac{1}{n-1}\sum (x_i - \bar x)^2$ | Average squared distance from the mean |
| Standard error | $\text{SE} = s/\sqrt{n}$ | How much the mean wobbles between samples |
| z-score | $z = (x - \mu)/\sigma$ | How many standard deviations from the mean |
| 95% CI for a mean | $\bar x \pm 1.96\,\text{SE}$ | Plausible range for the true mean |
| Correlation | $r = \frac{\text{cov}(x,y)}{s_x s_y}$ | Strength of a straight-line relationship |
| Bayes' rule | $P(A\mid B) = \frac{P(B\mid A)P(A)}{P(B)}$ | Update a belief with evidence |
| Linear regression | $\hat\beta = (X^\top X)^{-1}X^\top y$ | Best-fit coefficients |

## 📏 ML metrics formula sheet

| Metric | Formula | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| Accuracy | $\frac{TP+TN}{TP+TN+FP+FN}$ | Classes are balanced |
| Precision | $\frac{TP}{TP+FP}$ | False alarms are costly |
| Recall | $\frac{TP}{TP+FN}$ | Misses are costly |
| F1 | $2\cdot\frac{P\cdot R}{P+R}$ | You need one balanced number |
| MAE | $\frac{1}{n}\sum\lvert y-\hat y\rvert$ | Errors in the target's units |
| RMSE | $\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum (y-\hat y)^2}$ | Large errors matter more |
| MAPE | $\frac{100}{n}\sum\left\lvert\frac{y-\hat y}{y}\right\rvert$ | Percent error (avoid when $y \approx 0$) |
| $R^2$ | $1 - \frac{\sum (y-\hat y)^2}{\sum (y-\bar y)^2}$ | Share of variance explained |
| Log loss | $-\frac{1}{n}\sum [y\ln p + (1-y)\ln(1-p)]$ | Probabilities must be well calibrated |

: ML metrics {#tbl-metrics}

## 🎛️ Tool 1: metrics calculator

A model scores 1,000 simulated cases, 15% of which are positive. Move the **threshold** and watch the confusion matrix and every metric update.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import {ms, msStyle} from "/assets/js/ms-plot.js"
viewof thr = Inputs.range([0.05, 0.95], {value: 0.5, step: 0.01, label: "Decision threshold"})
viewof sep = Inputs.range([0.5, 3], {value: 1.6, step: 0.1, label: "Model quality (class separation)"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
cases = {
  const r = d3.randomNormal.source(d3.randomLcg(3)), out = [];
  const pos = r(sep, 1), neg = r(0, 1);
  for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i++) { const y = i < 150 ? 1 : 0; const z = y ? pos() : neg(); out.push({y, p: 1 / (1 + Math.exp(-(z - sep / 2) * 1.6))}); }
  return out;
}
{
  const TP = cases.filter(d => d.y && d.p >= thr).length, FN = 150 - TP;
  const FP = cases.filter(d => !d.y && d.p >= thr).length, TN = 850 - FP;
  const P = TP / Math.max(1, TP + FP), R = TP / 150, F1 = 2 * P * R / Math.max(1e-9, P + R), A = (TP + TN) / 1000;
  const cell = (v, label, c) => htl.html`<div style="background:${c};color:white;border-radius:12px;padding:14px;text-align:center"><div style="font-size:1.6rem;font-weight:700">${v}</div><div style="font-size:.85rem">${label}</div></div>`;
  return htl.html`<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:18px;align-items:start">
    <div><div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:8px">
      ${cell(TP, "✅ True positive", ms.teal)}${cell(FN, "❌ False negative (missed)", ms.rose)}
      ${cell(FP, "⚠️ False positive (false alarm)", ms.amber)}${cell(TN, "✅ True negative", ms.slate)}</div>
      <div style="font-size:.8rem;opacity:.7;margin-top:6px">Rows: actual positive / actual negative</div></div>
    ${Plot.plot({...msStyle, height: 200, width: 330, marginLeft: 80, x: {domain: [0, 1], label: null, grid: true}, y: {label: null},
      marks: [Plot.barX([{m: "Accuracy", v: A}, {m: "Precision", v: P}, {m: "Recall", v: R}, {m: "F1", v: F1}], {y: "m", x: "v", fill: ms.indigo, rx: 4}),
              Plot.text([{m: "Accuracy", v: A}, {m: "Precision", v: P}, {m: "Recall", v: R}, {m: "F1", v: F1}], {y: "m", x: "v", text: d => d.v.toFixed(2), dx: 16, fill: "currentColor"})]})}
  </div>`;
}
```

Notice that **accuracy stays high even at bad thresholds**, because 85% of cases are negative. That is why precision and recall exist.

## 🎛️ Tool 2: distribution explorer

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof dist = Inputs.radio(["Normal", "Binomial", "Poisson", "Exponential"], {value: "Normal", label: "Distribution"})
viewof p1 = Inputs.range([0.5, 20], {value: 5, step: 0.5, label: dist === "Normal" ? "Mean μ" : dist === "Binomial" ? "Trials n" : dist === "Poisson" ? "Rate λ" : "Rate λ (× 0.1)"})
viewof p2 = Inputs.range([0.05, 5], {value: 1.5, step: 0.05, label: dist === "Normal" ? "Std dev σ" : dist === "Binomial" ? "p (× 0.2)" : "unused"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const fact = k => k <= 1 ? 1 : k * fact(k - 1);
  let pts, discrete = false, note;
  if (dist === "Normal") { pts = d3.range(-5, 25.01, 0.1).map(x => ({x, y: Math.exp(-((x - p1) ** 2) / (2 * p2 * p2)) / (p2 * Math.sqrt(2 * Math.PI))})); note = "Heights, measurement errors, sums of many small effects"; }
  else if (dist === "Binomial") { const n = Math.round(p1), p = Math.min(0.99, p2 * 0.2); discrete = true; pts = d3.range(0, n + 1).map(k => ({x: k, y: fact(n) / (fact(k) * fact(n - k)) * p ** k * (1 - p) ** (n - k)})); note = `Successes in ${n} tries with p = ${p.toFixed(2)}: conversions, defects`; }
  else if (dist === "Poisson") { discrete = true; pts = d3.range(0, 41).map(k => ({x: k, y: Math.exp(-p1) * p1 ** k / fact(k)})); note = "Counts per interval: calls per hour, website errors per day"; }
  else { const l = p1 * 0.1; pts = d3.range(0, 25.01, 0.1).map(x => ({x, y: l * Math.exp(-l * x)})); note = "Waiting time between events: time to next customer"; }
  return htl.html`<div>${Plot.plot({...msStyle, height: 280, width: 760, marginLeft: 50, x: {label: "x →"}, y: {label: "↑ probability", grid: true},
    marks: [discrete ? Plot.barY(pts, {x: "x", y: "y", fill: ms.violet, rx: 2}) : Plot.areaY(pts, {x: "x", y: "y", fill: ms.violet, fillOpacity: 0.3}),
            discrete ? null : Plot.line(pts, {x: "x", y: "y", stroke: ms.violet, strokeWidth: 2.5})]})}
    <div class="ms-readout"><span>${dist}</span><b style="font-size:1rem">${note}</b></div></div>`;
}
```

## 🎛️ Tool 3: which statistical test?

```{mermaid}
%%| echo: false
flowchart TD
  A["❓ What are you comparing?"] --> B["Means of a numeric variable"]
  A --> C["Proportions or counts"]
  A --> D["Relationship between two numeric variables"]
  B --> B1{"How many groups?"}
  B1 -- "2" --> B2{"Same subjects twice?"}
  B2 -- yes --> T1["Paired t-test<br/>or Wilcoxon signed-rank"]
  B2 -- no --> T2["Welch t-test<br/>or Mann-Whitney U"]
  B1 -- "3+" --> T3["ANOVA<br/>or Kruskal-Wallis"]
  C --> C1{"Table size"}
  C1 -- "2 groups, yes/no" --> T4["Two-proportion z-test<br/>or Fisher exact"]
  C1 -- "larger table" --> T5["Chi-square test"]
  D --> T6["Pearson r, or Spearman<br/>if not linear"]
```

The second option in each box is the **non-parametric** version, safer when data are skewed or small. See our [p-value explainer](/statistics/hypothesis-testing/understanding-p-values.qmd) for what the result means.
